workplace-bullying-survivors-public-humi.headline: Workplace Bullying Survivors - Public Humiliation & Toxic Leadership
workplace-bullying-survivors-public-humi.author: Sabina Stanojevic, MBA
workplace-bullying-survivors-public-humi.core: Posted in last 7 days Workplace Bullying Survivors - Public Humiliation & Toxic Leadership I went out for brunch today. I left with a masterclass in toxic leadership. Beautiful venue. Strong reputation. Instagram - worthy branding. And an absolutely shocking reality behind the scenes. Today, I witnessed a manager publicly humiliating and intimidating a female employee in front of customers. A customer complained about a delayed order. Instead of handling the situation professionally, the manager started blaming the employee, sharing personal allegations about her behaviour and even claiming he had deliberately delayed an order to punish her. He then confronted her in the middle of the restaurant, in front of everyone. The irony? She was the ONLY employee who genuinely seemed to care about the customers and made an effort to communicate with us. As someone who has seen the world, with an MBA from Les Roches, and 3 degrees in total, with international expereince across luxury hospitality, commercial and technology environments, I find this behavious unacceptable. And as someone who has personally experienced workplace mobbing (not once), pychological and emotional abuse, this hit particularly close to home. Let's get something straight: → Feedback belongs behind closed doors, NOT in front of 30 customers. → Customer service recovery requires professionalism, NOT public humiliation. → Leadership is about accountability, NOT intimidation. → Employee experience IS customer experience. You can invest millions in branding, marketing and beautiful interiors. But how you treat your employees reveals the REAL culture behind your business. Today reinforced a long-term ambition of mine: combining international business, coaching, somatic approaches and advocacy to eventually build something bigger than myself: an educational and healing platform, a media company talking about the TRUTH. Potentially an institute dedicated to protecting human dignity and addressing workplace abuse, particularly against women. Because nobody should have to sacrifice their mental health, dignity or livelihood just to earn a living. And now I want to hear from YOU. Have you ever experienced workplace mobbing, public humiliation, psychological abuse or intimidation by someone in a position of power? Did anyone protect you? Or were you left to fight for yourself? I'm looking to connect with people willing to share their experiences and participate in interviews as I explore how to turn awareness into meaningful change. My inbox is open. Your story matters. And to every leader reading this: Your job is to lead people. Not to break them. #ToxicLeadership #WorkplaceBullying #HospitalityLeadership #EmployeeExperience #WomenAtWork #Leadership

african-diaspora-identity-and-migration-.headline: African Diaspora - Identity & Migration Across Generations
african-diaspora-identity-and-migration-.author: Jennifer Eze
african-diaspora-identity-and-migration-.core: Posted in last 7 days African Diaspora - Identity & Migration Across Generations i'm exploring something new, and i think it's time to put it out into the world i'm building an independent editorial project exploring african identity, migration and belonging across generations and geographical borders and this one is quite personal to me. my parents migrated from nigeria to the uk in search of a better future, as many african families have done i was born and raised here, but grew up with nigeria very much at the centre of my upbringing. (if you know me well enough, you'll know just how much of my personality and mannerisms are rooted in nigerian culture 😭) but as i've grown older, i've found myself asking questions that i don't think i've fully answered. what does it mean to belong to a place? why do so many people feel they have to leave their home countries to access the opportunities they want? what happens when the country you call home doesn't always make you feel at home? and how do we create societies where people genuinely have the choice to build fulfilling lives, wherever they come from? these aren't questions with straightforward answers and that's quite literally the point. i don't believe one person, one experience or one perspective can speak for an entire continent or community. but i do believe there's so much we can learn when we make room for different voices. recent conversations have reminded me just how many people have their own experiences to share, perspectives to challenge and questions that deserve to be explored. because behind every statistic is a person, a family and a story that deserves to be understood. and these conversations shouldn't end at awareness. they should challenge our assumptions, encourage us to question the societies we live in and, hopefully, inspire meaningful change. so, introducing: Where Do We Belong? through personal stories, interviews, research, articles and roundtable discussions, i hope to explore the experiences of african people across different countries, generations and walks of life. from those who have migrated, stayed or returned, to those growing up in the diaspora and navigating multiple cultural identities. and importantly, i don't want these conversations to focus solely on the challenges we face. there's so much to celebrate, question and understand about our cultures, ambitions, achievements, communities and the futures we're building. if any of this resonates with you, i'd love to hear from you! whether you have a perspective you'd like to share, experience in research, writing or community-building, or simply an interest in the conversations we're hoping to create, please feel free to connect or drop me a message this is still very much in its early stages, but i'm excited to see what we can build through the perspectives and experiences of others. where do we belong?

african-communities-facing-climate-impac.headline: African Communities Facing Climate Impacts - COP31 Voices
african-communities-facing-climate-impac.author: Ayooluwa Ogunsola
african-communities-facing-climate-impac.core: Posted in last 7 days African Communities Facing Climate Impacts - COP31 Voices Why am I going to COP31? Because over the past year, I have visited more communities directly affected by the climate crisis than the average person probably ever will. I have sat with people, listened to their stories, documented some of their experiences and, at other times, simply listened quietly. From communities facing displacement and environmental destruction to people whose livelihoods, homes and futures are being threatened, I have seen that the impacts of the climate crisis are not just environmental. They are economic, social, cultural and deeply human. I am going to COP31 because these experiences should not end as stories told in affected communities. They deserve to be heard where decisions are made. Too often, the people making decisions are far removed from the realities of those living with the consequences. And even when affected communities want to reach their leaders, the bureaucracy, access barriers and complicated processes can make it incredibly difficult. I don’t want COP31 to be another space where people talk about communities without actually listening to them. So, from 9–21 November, I want to hear from you. Wherever you are in Africa, reach out to me. I will be in the comments and my DMs will be open. What struggles is your community facing because of the climate crisis? What stories do you think the world needs to hear? Which leaders, institutions or decision-makers do you want to reach? What would you want them to know if you had the opportunity to speak directly to them? I may not have all the answers, and I cannot promise to solve every problem. But I can listen, ask questions, document experiences and find ways to bring these realities into conversations happening at COP31. I cannot claim to speak for everyone I meet. But I can help create more space for their voices to be heard

multilingual-leaders-and-introverts-spea.headline: Multilingual Leaders & Introverts - Speaking Up in English at Work
multilingual-leaders-and-introverts-spea.author: Louise Jefferies
multilingual-leaders-and-introverts-spea.core: Posted in last 7 days Multilingual Leaders & Introverts - Speaking Up in English at Work What if the problem isnt your English, your expertise or your ability, but what happens when you have to use them under pressure? I'm starting Season 2 ofEnglish Talk: Speaking up in English at Work, and I'm changing the format. Throughout November, Ill be sharing a three-part conversation with Fatima-Zohra MENAS, MD, MSc, exploring something I see again and again in my work with multilingual professionals. Capable people who know their subject, have years of experience and have plenty to contribute, yet find it difficult to speak up when it matters. Sometimes they worry about finding the right words. Sometimes they go blank, overthink what they want to say or fear being judged. Sometimes, they assume that if they were really good at their jobs, their work would speak for itself... But communication is about more than just language. In my conversation with Fatima, we explore: 🎙️The fear of getting what you want. Why an opportunity you've worked towards can trigger anxiety when it finally arrives 🎙️Why your English isn't the whole story. What else can get in the way when you know your subject but struggle to make your contribution heard. 🎙️You don't need to become someone else to lead. How the qualities you've underestimated in yourself can actually be strengths when you learn to use them differently, These conversations are primarily about confidence, visibility and leadership, but also about the assumptions we make about ourselves and what we believe were capable of doing, because I don't believe you need to become louder, more extroverted or a different person to speak up with confidence. You just need to understand what's getting in your way and learn how to access the capabilities you already have when the situation demands it. I'll be sharing the three episodes throughout November, listen via my website, or wherever you listen to your podcasts. Season 2 Episode 1 Part 1 out now Link in the comments and in the featured posts of my profile. ______________________________________________ Want to join the conversation? If you're a multilingual leader or an introvert who's overcome the struggle to feel comfortable in the spotlight and you'd like to share your story with me and my audience, I'd love to hear from you!
